targets.authors: Clark, C. J., Luguri, J. B., Ditto, P. H., Knobe, J., Shariff, A. F., & Baumeister, R. F.
targets.title: Free to punish: A motivated account of free will belief.
targets.evidence_quote: Studies 1 and 2b are exact replications of Clark et al.’s (2014) Studies 1 and 2, respectively, and our Study 2a is a close replication of Clark et al. (2014) Study 2 (we use identical measures and procedures, but a different sample population).
targets.outcome_quote: Across replication experiments we found no evidence for the original claim that witnessing immoral behavior causes people to increase their belief in free will, though we did replicate the finding that people attribute more free will to agents who behave immorally compared to a neutral control (Studies 2a & 3).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors report failure of general free-will belief effects and replication of agent-specific attributions, with contrasting support within the same original paper. Study 3 also re-tests the agent-specific contrast while extending its explanation.

reasoning: Full preprint title and authors match assigned published article. Only Clark et al. 2014 is directly retested; other attribution and free-will papers motivate theoretical accounts, not new replication targets.
